What is dashboard_vrtl?

dashboard_vrtl is an enterprise BI platform built for Odoo. It lets you create interactive dashboards with charts, KPIs, alerts, and drill-down navigation — all from within Odoo, using Odoo data.

Why dashboard_vrtl?

Odoo has reports and pivot tables — but no real dashboard builder. dashboard_vrtl fills that gap:

  • 18+ chart types — bar, line, pie, funnel, sankey, treemap, and more
  • Semantic metrics — define "Revenue" once, use it everywhere
  • Cross-chart interactivity — click a region, all charts filter
  • Threshold alerts — get notified when stock drops below 10
  • Dashboard-as-code — version your dashboards in Git
  • AI-assisted — describe what you want, the AI builds it

Course overview

  1. Core Models — Understanding dashboards, metrics, charts
  2. Metrics & Data Sources — Connecting to Odoo data
  3. Building Dashboards — Step-by-step guide
  4. Alerts & Security — Notifications and access control
  5. Dashboard-as-Code — YAML, version control, deployment

Time: ~45 minutes | Level: Beginner to Intermediate

How dashboard_vrtl is built

dashboard_vrtl is modular — a core platform with domain-specific extensions:

ModulePurpose
dashboard_vrtlCore: models, UI, alerts, caching
dashboard_vrtl_salesPre-built sales dashboards
dashboard_vrtl_financePre-built finance dashboards
dashboard_vrtl_source_finance52 financial report adapters
dashboard_vrtl_taxonomySwedish XBRL taxonomy integration
dashboard_vrtl_lmsThis course!

The three-layer architecture

  1. Metrics — Define what you measure (Revenue, Orders, Stock Level). One definition, used everywhere.
  2. Sources — Where data comes from (Odoo model, SQL query, or external adapter).
  3. Charts — How you visualize it (bar, line, KPI, table). Many charts can share one metric.

Data flow

Metric → _read_group() → cache → chart → amCharts 5

Metrics use Odoo's built-in _read_group() for database-level aggregation. Results are cached per user and per filter combination. Charts render with amCharts 5 — the same library powering professional BI tools.

Dashboard → Metric → Chart

Everything in dashboard_vrtl revolves around three models:

1. Dashboard (dashboard.dashboard)

  • A container for charts, filters, and alerts
  • Has access control (groups or users)
  • Auto-refresh every N seconds/minutes
  • Appears as a menu item in Odoo

2. Metric (dashboard.metric)

  • Defines what you measure
  • Example: "Net Revenue = SUM of sale.order.amount_total where state is not draft/cancel"
  • Four source types: model, sql, service, composite
  • A metric is reusable — one metric can power many charts

3. Chart (dashboard.chart)

  • Connects a metric to a visualization
  • 18+ chart types: bar, line, pie, funnel, sankey, treemap, KPI, table...
  • Has grouping, sorting, limits, and drill-down configuration
  • Per-chart access control (chart_group_ids)

How they connect

Dashboard → contains → Charts → reference → Metrics

One Metric can power multiple Charts on different Dashboards. Change the Metric definition once — all Charts update.

Defining a Metric

A metric answers one question: "What is X?"

Metric fields that matter

  • source_type: model (Odoo model), sql (custom query), service (adapter), composite (formula)
  • model_id / field_id: Which Odoo model and field to measure
  • aggregation: sum, avg, count, min, max
  • default_domain: Always-active filters, e.g. exclude drafts and cancellations
  • date_field_id: Which field is the "time" dimension
  • unit: monetary, percentage, integer, float

Example: Net Revenue Metric

FieldValue
nameNet Revenue
keysales.net_revenue
source_typemodel
model_idsale.order
field_idamount_total
aggregationsum
default_domain[['state','not in',['draft','cancel']]]
date_field_iddate_order
unitmonetary

Metric key — why it matters

The key field is a unique identifier like "sales.net_revenue". It's used for:

  • Cross-referencing in YAML dashboard definitions
  • Composite metrics (formulas reference keys)
  • Dashboard-as-code portability across instances

Creating your first dashboard

Via the Odoo UI

  1. Go to BI Dashboard → Dashboards → Create
  2. Fill in:
    • Name: "My Sales Dashboard"
    • Key: "my_sales" (unique identifier)
    • Category: "Sales"
    • Auto-Refresh: 5 Minutes
    • Cache TTL: 300 (seconds)
  3. Under Access, set who can view it
  4. Under Menu, choose where it appears in the Odoo menu
  5. Click Save

Via YAML (dashboard-as-code)

Create a file my_sales.yaml:

dashboard:
  key: my_sales
  name: "My Sales Dashboard"
  category: Sales
  auto_refresh: 300000
  cache_ttl: 300

filters:
  - key: period
    type: date_range
    label: "Period"
    default:
      from: this_month_start
      to: today

Then load it: Dashboard.load_from_module_yaml('my_module', 'data/my_sales.yaml')

Creating your first metric

Metric: Net Revenue

Go to BI Dashboard → Metrics → Create and fill in:

FieldValueWhy
NameNet RevenueHuman-readable name
Keysales.net_revenueUnique identifier
Source TypeOdoo ModelSimple model binding
Modelsale.orderSales orders table
Fieldamount_totalTotal order amount
AggregationSumAdd all amounts
UnitMonetaryDisplay as currency
Date Fielddate_orderTime dimension
Domain[['state','not in',['draft','cancel']]]Exclude drafts

What happens behind the scenes

When this metric is queried, dashboard_vrtl calls:

self.env['sale.order']._read_group(
    domain=[('state','not in',['draft','cancel'])],
    groupby=[],
    aggregates=['amount_total:sum'],
)

This runs a single SQL query with GROUP BY in the database — not Python loops!

Security auto-detection

dashboard_vrtl automatically checks if the model has ir.rules and sets row_level_security=True. This means each user sees only their authorized data.

Adding charts to your dashboard

Now that you have a dashboard and a metric, let's add visualizations.

Chart 1: Revenue KPI

Go to BI Dashboard → Charts → Create:

FieldValue
NameRevenue (KPI)
DashboardMy Sales Dashboard
MetricNet Revenue
Chart TypeKPI
ComparisonPrevious Period (%)

Chart 2: Revenue Trend (Line Chart)

FieldValue
NameRevenue Trend
DashboardMy Sales Dashboard
MetricNet Revenue
Chart TypeLine Chart
Group Bydate_order
Time RangeMonth
Limit12 (rolling 12 months)

Chart 3: Top Products (Bar Chart)

Create a second metric first for product revenue:

  • Model: sale.order.line
  • Field: price_subtotal
  • Group By: product_id

Then create the chart with Bar Chart type, limit 5, sort descending.

Layout tips

  • Put KPIs at the top (w=2-3, h=2)
  • Main chart in the center (w=6, h=4)
  • Supplementary charts on the right or bottom
  • Max ~8-12 charts per dashboard

Making dashboards interactive

Global Filters

Add a filter that affects all compatible charts:

  1. Go to your dashboard, scroll to the Filters tab
  2. Add a filter:
    • Key: "period"
    • Type: Date Range
    • Default From: "this_month_start"
    • Default To: "today"
    • Shortcuts: [{"label":"This Month","from":"this_month_start","to":"today"}]

Now a filter bar appears above your charts. Change the period — all charts update together.

Cross-Chart Filtering

Single-click any chart element to filter the entire dashboard:

  • Click "Nord" in a pie chart → all charts filter to Nord region
  • Click "Product A" → both Nord and Product A filters stack
  • Click ✕ on a filter badge to remove it

Drill-Down

Double-click a chart element to drill into details:

  • Double-click "Nord" → see products within Nord
  • Double-click "Product A" → see customers who bought it
  • Breadcrumbs show: Dashboard > Nord > Product A
  • Click any breadcrumb to go back

Filter compatibility

Not all charts support all filters. A P&L statement doesn't have a "customer" filter — it simply ignores incompatible filters. No errors, no confusion.

Get notified when things matter

Alerts monitor a metric and trigger when a condition is met.

Creating an alert

Go to BI Dashboard → Alert Rules → Create:

FieldValueNotes
NameLow Stock AlertDescriptive name
MetricStock LevelWhat to monitor
Conditionvalue < 10Triggers when stock < 10
SeverityWarningInfo / Warning / Critical
Schedule0 */4 * * *Every 4 hours
Cooldown3600Min 1 hour between alerts
Channelsnotification, activityWhere to notify

Condition syntax

Available variables:

  • value — current metric value
  • previous_value — value from last evaluation
  • delta — percentage change: ((value - previous) / previous) * 100

Examples:

  • value < 10 — simple threshold
  • delta < -30 and value < 50000 — sharp drop AND low baseline
  • value >= 1000000 — exceeded target

Notification Channels

  • notification: Message in Odoo Discuss "Dashboard Alerts" channel
  • activity: Task in recipient's "To-Do" list — requires acknowledgment

Anti-flood protection

  • Cooldown: Minimum seconds between repeated alerts
  • State machine: ok → triggered → acknowledged → ok
  • Auto-reset: If condition is no longer met, alert auto-resolves

Four layers of security

1. User Groups (who can even open the menu?)

  • group_dashboard_user: View dashboards assigned to you
  • group_dashboard_manager: Create, edit, delete dashboards

2. Dashboard-Level Access

  • access_by: "Access Groups" or "Users"
  • group_ids / user_ids: Who can see this dashboard
  • Empty = open to all users

3. Chart-Level Access

  • chart_group_ids: Only these groups see this chart
  • Example: "KPI: Margin" visible only to Managers
  • Enforced via ir.rule — not just frontend hiding

4. Row-Level Data Security

  • Odoo ir.rules applied automatically for model-based metrics
  • Sales rep only sees their team's data
  • CFO sees all companies
  • SQL metrics use security bridge: WHERE id = ANY(authorized_ids)

Cache Security

Cached data includes the user's ID in the cache key — one user can never see another user's data through the cache.

Dashboard-as-Code — Version Your Dashboards

Instead of clicking through the UI, you can define dashboards in YAML files. This gives you:

  • Version control — track changes in Git
  • Code review — PR before deploying
  • Reproducibility — same dashboard in dev, staging, prod
  • Portability — deploy to multiple Odoo instances

Complete YAML Example

dashboard:
  key: cfo_daily
  name: "CFO Daily Dashboard"
  category: Finance
  auto_refresh: 900000

filters:
  - key: period
    type: date_range
    label: "Period"
    default: {from: this_month_start, to: today}

metrics:
  - key: finance.revenue
    label: "Revenue"
    source_type: model
    model: account.move.line
    field: credit
    aggregation: sum
    unit: monetary
    date_field: date
    domain:
      - [parent_state, "=", posted]
      - [account_id.account_type, in, [income, income_other]]

charts:
  - key: kpi_revenue
    type: kpi
    metric: finance.revenue
    label: "Revenue"
    layout: {x: 0, y: 0, w: 3, h: 2}
    comparison: previous_period

  - key: chart_trend
    type: line
    metric: finance.revenue
    label: "Revenue Trend"
    layout: {x: 0, y: 2, w: 6, h: 4}
    config:
      group_by: date:month

Loading YAML

In your module's data XML:

<function model="dashboard.dashboard"
    name="load_from_module_yaml"
    eval="['my_module', 'data/my_dashboard.yaml']"/>

AI-Assisted Dashboard Creation

dashboard_vrtl includes an AI skill (SKILL.md). Just describe what you want:

"I need a sales dashboard showing net revenue per month, top 5 products, and an alert when daily revenue drops 30% below average."

The AI will generate the complete YAML for you.
Test your understanding of dashboard_vrtl core concepts.
What are the three core models in dashboard_vrtl?
Correct! Dashboard contains Charts, Charts reference Metrics, Metrics define the data.
These are standard Odoo features. dashboard_vrtl uses Dashboard, Metric, and Chart.
These are supporting models. The core three are Dashboard, Metric, and Chart.
Which metric source_type should you use for a simple SUM of a sale.order field?
Correct! Use model for direct Odoo model bindings. It uses _read_group() for database-level aggregation.
SQL is for complex queries that _read_group() can't handle. Simple aggregations should use model.
Composite is for formulas combining multiple metrics, e.g. revenue / orders.
Which condition triggers an alert when a metric drops more than 30% compared to its previous value?
Correct! delta is the percentage change from the previous evaluation.
This checks if the value is less than -30 (a negative number), not a 30% drop.
Close but not necessary — use the simpler delta < -30 instead.
How does dashboard_vrtl prevent one user from seeing another user's data through the cache?
Cache key includes user_id for row-level security metrics
Correct! user_id is part of the SHA-256 cache key, so different users get different cache entries.
All cache entries are encrypted per user
Encryption is not used. The cache key contains the user_id, making separate entries.
What happens when you single-click a chart element in dashboard_vrtl?
All compatible charts on the dashboard are filtered by the clicked value
Correct! This is cross-chart filtering — the core interactivity feature.
The clicked chart zooms in to show details (drill-down)
Drill-down is double-click, not single-click. Single-click filters the entire dashboard.
Only the clicked chart updates; other charts stay the same
All compatible charts update together. Incompatible charts (e.g. P&L with no region filter) stay unchanged.
